title: Formation of water
explanation: Hydrogen and oxygen combine to form water. Very exothermic – this is a theoretical example.

title: Combustion of methane
explanation: Natural gas burns in plenty of oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water.

title: Combustion of propane
explanation: LPG burning in a gas stove.

title: Acid–base neutralisation
explanation: H⁺ from the acid and OH⁻ from the base form water; the spectator ions make the salt.

title: Photosynthesis (overall)
explanation: Plants store light energy as glucose. This overall equation summarises many steps.

title: Aerobic respiration (overall)
explanation: Cells release energy from glucose – the reverse of photosynthesis.

title: Thermal decomposition of limestone
explanation: Used to make quicklime in a lime kiln.

title: Rusting of iron (simplified)
explanation: Iron is oxidised. Real rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide.

title: Zinc with hydrochloric acid
explanation: A reactive metal displaces hydrogen from an acid.

title: Iron displaces copper
explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces it – a copper coating appears.

title: Silver chloride precipitate
explanation: Mixing the solutions forms a white precipitate of AgCl – a test for chloride ions.

title: Haber process
explanation: Industrial ammonia synthesis; a reversible reaction.

title: Electrolysis of water
explanation: Two volumes of hydrogen form at the cathode for every one volume of oxygen at the anode.

title: Baking soda and vinegar
explanation: The fizzing is carbon dioxide gas.
